reasons: The measured result is economically meaningless as presented: net_pnl_points is -8,194,366 with gross_pnl_points -8,185,725, i.e. the strategy lost money before any costs, yet the primary score is -0.0488 and the campaign treats it as the best of nine trials. A negative score paired with a massively negative net P&L means the score is not measuring money made; whatever the ratio is rewarding (inactivity, exposure, scale artifacts), it is not profitability.

The P&L units are incoherent with the instrument. The evidence is labeled 'NQ is $20 per index point' and 'commission_per_contract_per_side_points: 0.0', but the strategy and pre-registration are BTC-USDT perpetuals on OKX with fees quoted in basis points of notional (0 bp maker / 2 bp taker). There is no mapping from the reported 'index points' to BTC price moves, so the magnitude of the loss cannot be interpreted at all — it is not knowable whether -8.19M points is a rounding error or total ruin.

Commission is charged on every fill per the evidence header, yet commission_per_contract_per_side_points is 0.0 while commission_paid_points is 8,641. The cost model that produced the outcome is internally inconsistent, so 'earns money after fees' — the pre-registered success criterion — cannot be evaluated from this evidence.

The strategy's own docstring reports every prior trial scoring between -0.068 and -0.438 and this winner at -0.068 to -0.048; no trial was ever positive. The campaign's conclusion is that the family loses money, which is a legitimate research finding but is not a trading edge, and the evidence as given does not support presenting it as one.
auditors.confidence_note: I could not see the backtest engine, the fill simulator, or any per-session P&L breakdown, so I cannot tell whether the -8.19M figure is a unit-scaling bug, a sign error, or a genuine catastrophic loss; either way the reported economics are not interpretable as given.

reasons: Breadth signals conflict: month breadth is acceptable (15/32 positive, 47%) but weekday breadth is narrow (2/7 positive — only Tue +521K and Wed +1.92M; Mon/Thu/Fri/Sat/Sun all negative, Sun -3.17M) and hour breadth is narrow (4/24 positive). The seasonality_caveat explicitly warns that on this dataset hour-of-day (and by extension weekday) may be arithmetic on a drifting session index carrying no regime information, so I cannot confirm the weekday/hour narrowness is a real distributional finding or a calendar artifact.

Profitability is front-loaded on the reliable month axis (2023 +713K, 2024 -1.78M, 2025 -7.13M; only 1 of 8 months in 2025 positive). This is either regime/time confinement (a robustness finding) or ordinary performance decay (another axis's concern); with no out-of-sample run I cannot distinguish the two.

The 'held up by a minority / single session' veto is NOT met: best_session_share is only 2.45%, top-5% concentration is 40%, and the rule acts broadly (39,381 trades across 960 sessions with exposure), so there is no single-trade or single-session dependence to point to.
auditors.confidence_note: No validation was run and I cannot verify whether the narrow weekday/hour breakdowns carry real regime information or are calendar artifacts, so I cannot resolve whether the result is genuinely narrow or merely unevenly distributed.
